summary.headline: UTI AMC FY26 standalone normalized PAT fell to Rs 643 crore from Rs 653 crore, while core PAT rose to Rs 460 crore from Rs 447 crore.
summary.overview: UTI AMC reported FY26 standalone core income of Rs 1,255 crore (up from Rs 1,180 crore) and normalized core PAT of Rs 460 crore (up from Rs 447 crore). Consolidated normalized PAT fell to Rs 511 crore from Rs 731 crore, and consolidated normalized core PAT fell to Rs 452 crore from Rs 492 crore. Costs rose sharply: consolidated Q4 employee cost of Rs 132 crore was up about 14% YoY even after a one-time VRS and family pension charge of about Rs 130 crore taken in Q3. The company declared a Rs 40 per share FY26 dividend and management said it sees the payout trend at about 95% of profits. Management's single stated priority is growth in MF AUM, with cost discipline as the second.

segments.name: UTI Mutual Fund (AMC)
segments.commentary: Gross sales market share of 5.5% in Q4 and 6.1% in FY26. Equity quarterly average AUM Rs 95,824 crore in March 2026, up 5.46% YoY. Index and ETF quarterly average AUM Rs 1,76,673 crore, up 24.86% in Q4.

segments.name: UTI Pension Fund (100% subsidiary)
segments.commentary: AUM Rs 4.02 lakh crore, up 11.8% YoY (about 12% per subsidiary slide), holding 24.36% of NPS industry AUM. Private sector pension AUM grew 46% YoY; AMC retained EPFO and CMPFO mandates for 5-year tenures.

segments.name: UTI Alternatives
segments.commentary: AUM Rs 5,280 crore across five active funds. SDOF-II fully exited with 13.4% IRR; SDOF-IV launched in Q2 with Rs 674 crore AUM against a Rs 1,500 crore plus Rs 500 crore greenshoe target.

segments.name: UTI International
segments.commentary: AUM USD 1.74 billion (Rs 16,144 crore) at March 2026. Management described the segment as under pressure from foreign outflows (about USD 40 billion out of India in CY25 and Q1 CY26) and a 9% rupee depreciation over the year.

guidance_outlook: Standalone employee cost run rate guided at Rs 90-95 crore per quarter; consolidated at Rs 125-130 crore per quarter, higher due to capability build-out in all three businesses.
Standalone other administrative expenses guided to rise about 7-8% (around 8% cited); consolidated 100-200 bps higher, around 10%, due to UTI Pension Fund geographic expansion.

Weighted average yield expected to dilute by about 1-2 bps in FY27 from a mix shift toward ETFs, index funds and low-duration debt funds. Current yield breakup: equity and hybrid 75 bps, ETF and index about 8 bps, cash and arbitrage about 10 bps, income funds 18-19 bps, blended about 32 bps.
Passive pipeline: filings planned for UTI NIFTY 500 Index Fund, UTI BSE Index Sector Leaders, UTI NIFTY India New Age Consumption and UTI NIFTY India Internet Fund, each in index and ETF form.
At least one SIF product targeted for launch in the current year; GIFT City retail FME licence received for UTI Alternatives.
Management does not expect to add to the cash pile and will continue paying out most earnings as dividends.
capex_capacity: Around 270 branches and about 260 UFCs (unique feet-on-street); about 90 UFCs added in the last 1.5 years, and management says RM count is largely fully staffed.
Employee count fell to 1,248 at March 2026 from 1,402 at March 2024; supervisor-to-RM ratio improved from about 1:1 to 1:5.
Cloud infrastructure upgrade added about Rs 8 crore to other expenses in FY26.
Management says it is operating below capacity and expects operating leverage as the cost base is absorbed.
demand_pricing: Industry AUM Rs 79.46 lakh crore and total folios 27.39 crore at March 2026; SIP contribution Rs 32,087 crore in March 2026, with SIP AUM about Rs 15 lakh crore (19.94% share).
UTI SIP inflows Rs 9,442 crore in FY26 (up 13.42% vs Rs 8,325 crore); Q4 SIP inflows Rs 2,457 crore; SIP AUM Rs 39,813 crore (up 5.91%); active SIP folios 29.53 lakh (up 9.71%).
Net equity flows were close to zero in FY26 after negative flows in the prior two years; 8 of 19 core funds recorded positive net sales.
FY26 new investor PANs added: 7.16 lakh, taking total folios to 1.38 crore; 76% of 14.5 lakh gross new SIP registrations were digital.
Banking channel share of equity and hybrid float about 1.5%. Management is focusing on banks and fintechs, with fintech traction among Gen Z investors starting at Rs 1,000-1,500 SIP tickets.
Product launch: UTI Multicap Fund raised about Rs 1,000 crore; UTI Arbitrage Fund crossed Rs 10,000 crore AUM. Passive AUM Rs 24,897 crore (ETF Rs 18,963 crore, index Rs 5,934 crore).

qa_highlights.question: What was the one-off in Q4/FY26 expenses, and how should employee and other expenses be modelled for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about Rs 130 crore of VRS and family pension one-off was provided in Q3 FY26, plus about Rs 4 crore for the Labour Code. Analyst noted consolidated Q4 employee cost of Rs 132 crore was still up 14% YoY; management attributed this to variable pay and recruitment across three businesses. FY27 guidance: standalone employee cost Rs 90-95 crore per quarter, consolidated Rs 125-130 crore; other admin expenses +7-8% standalone and about 10% consolidated.

qa_highlights.question: How did customer acquisition go during the March volatility, and what schemes attract first-time SIP investors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no sharp pick-up in new investors in March; SIP stoppages rose seasonally. February new SIP additions were better than the industry. First-time investors mainly choose index funds, often with Rs 1,000-1,500 SIP tickets. New PAN acquisition is now a sales metric, with FY26 target to grow the 7.16 lakh count.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of SEBI's revised norms from 1 April, and what is the yield outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Exit load TER cut by 5 bps, plus some base TER rationalisation; management expects the impact to pass through to intermediaries and sees no effect on AMC yield. Yield may dilute by 1-2 bps in FY27 due to mix shift to ETFs and low-duration debt.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan to return equity net sales to positive territory?
qa_highlights.answer: Priority is raising SIP book. Management is repositioning sales teams to sell multiple funds across value, GARP and quality growth styles, to reduce pro-cyclicality to performance. Net equity flows were close to zero in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the employee count fall while sales staff grows, and is RM headcount rising further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the mix is being corrected toward revenue-generating roles. It does not expect RM count to rise much further from about 260 UFCs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for international business and SIF launches?
qa_highlights.answer: International AUM is under pressure from foreign outflows and currency weakness; management plans to hold ground and bring institutional clients into alternatives. SIF: at least one fund targeted this year, first product unlikely to be priced above plain-vanilla MF yields; higher yield depends on long-short differentiation.

qa_highlights.question: How should the Rs 4,000-4,500 crore cash and investments be deployed, and what is the dividend policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no plans for cash build-up or buybacks; cash retained for liquidity and possible M&A. Dividend trend line is roughly 95% payout including Rs 40 per share for FY26. Business described as not capital-intensive.

risks_watch: Consolidated normalized PAT fell about 30% YoY to Rs 511 crore, and consolidated employee and admin costs are guided to keep rising in FY27.
Equity net flows close to zero in FY26; the shift toward SIPs and multi-fund selling is unproven.
Fund performance: management acknowledged quality growth and GARP funds underperformed due to market season, and some execution improvement is needed.
International business under pressure from foreign outflows and rupee weakness; no clear recovery timeline given.
Yield dilution of 1-2 bps expected in FY27 from asset mix shift.
SEBI TER and exit-load changes effective 1 April; full impact still to be seen.
Watch Q1 FY27 SIP stoppage ratios, new PAN additions versus 7.16 lakh in FY26, and whether consolidated cost guidance holds.

But managing yield for the sake of managing yield is not a thing that I am in favo ur of. I would rather manage revenue.
So, right now, I would say it's just to hold our ground.
I think roughly we are at about 95% almost in terms of a trend line.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on growth ambitions and the capital return stance, citing a diversified fund platform and a dividend trend line of about 95%. It was cautious and somewhat evasive on fund underperformance, near-zero equity net flows, the international business, and SIF pricing, attributing these mainly to market seasons and foreign outflows with no firm recovery timeline.
